Explore Microsoft Copilot Studio and agent harnesses

Learning Path-1: Get started with Ai-first solutions

  • Microsoft redesigned Power Platform around an AI-first philosophy.
  • Power Platform consists of 6 components: Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages, Microsoft Copilot Studio, AI Builder and Power BI.

Understand Component Purpose

  1. PowerApps:

    • Build custom user interfaces
    • Control over screen layout and mobile-friendly experiences

  2. Power Automate

    • Handles process automation and integration.
    • Cloud flows orchestrate logic across connectors and services.
    • Built-in approval actions create structured human-in-the-loop experience.

  3. Microsoft Copilot Studio

    • to build conversational and autonomous agents.
    • autonomous agents respond to triggers such as a new record, scheduled time, incoming email.
    • process requires natural language interaction or without constant human input.

  4. AI Builder

    • Provides pretrained AI models and a prompt-building environment.

  5. Power Pages

    • External facing web experience.
    • Provides configurable web portal with secure authentication.

Microsoft Foundry Basics:

Foundry RBAC roles:

  1. Foundry User
  2. Foundry Owner
  3. Foundry Account Owner
  4. Foundry Project Manager

Path for new developers:

Steps:

  1. Install 'Foundry Toolkit for VS Code' from "https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-windows-ai-studio.windows-ai-studio".
  2. Install Azure Developer CLI (azd) from "https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/install-azd?tabs=winget-windows%2Cbrew-mac%2Cscript-linux&pivots=os-windows"
  3. Install every Foundry extension in one step through the meta-package: azd ext install microsoft.foundry in Command Prompt terminal
  4. Install Microsoft Foundry Canvas

Microsoft Foundry Canvas

  • Microsoft Foundry Canvas is a GitHub Copilot App extension that is used to design, configure, test and deploy Foundry hosted agents from a side panel.

The New Copilot Studio Experience

Model

  • The following models are listed in the new experience:
    • Managed models such as the GPT-5 and Anthropic models.

Channels

  • It defines where the users can interact with the agent.
  • There are two ways to add an agent to a web app- The embed code can be added to any HTML web app, Using Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, and Agents Client SDK for native apps using iOS, Android and Windows.
  • The options include Teams+Microsoft 365, Demo website and App Embeds.

Skills

  • It defines the behaviors through structured instructions
  • There are 2 ways to add a skill: Upload a skill and Create from blank.
  • To upload a skill, the uploaded file must be a "SKILL.md" file or zip that includes SKILL.md
  • The SKILL.md file must contain the skill name and description formatted in YAML.
  • When creating from blank, you need to input the name of the skill, give a description of what the skill does and when to use it and instructions when the skill is activated.

Tools

  • It gives tools to connect the agent to external systems and actions.
  • Featured tools include Office 365 Outlook, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive for Business, Excel Online (Business) and Microsoft Dataverse.
  • Different tools can be added such as Model Context Protocol, Connectors, Workflows.
  • Under Workflows, only those are supported which have the "When an agent calls the workflow" trigger.

Knowledge

  • It provides trusted context to guide decisions.
  • It helps the agent provide more relevant information and insights.
  • Featured knowledge sources are: Public websites, SharePoint, OneDrive for Business, Salesforce, Azure SQL

Everything Start to Finish

Create an agent

  • You can change the primary language, solution and schema name for the agent.
  • The description can have up to 1024 characters.
  • To change agent's introduction: System topic -> Conversation Start -> Message node
  • We can configure up to 10 suggested prompts that users can from to start a conversation with the agent. It isnt visible when testing the agent.

Everything Topics:

  1. To respond to users, agents use either generative orchestration or classic orchestration.
  2. In generative orchestrations, agent selects the most appropriate combination of topics, tools and knowledge. Each topic has a description to inform the agent its purpose.
  3. In classic orchestration, each topic has trigger phrases, keywords and questions that is likely to match with user input. Agents use Natural Language Understanding the select the topic.
  4. A topic contains one or more nodes and determines the conversational paths.
  5. There are 2 kinds of topics: System and Custom topics.
  6. System topics cant be created, deleted but can be turned off.
  7. Types of nodes: Message, Question, Adaptive Card, Condition, Variable Management, Topic Management, Tool, HTTP requests.
  8. Node name can be up to 500 characters in length.
  9. The topics can be edited with YAML code editor.

Everything Knowledge

  1. Agents can use enterprise data from Power Platform, Dynamics 365 data, websites and external systems.
  2. At agent level we can use knowledge from Knowledge page but at the topic level, we can use generative answers node for knowledge.
  3. Supported knowledge sources are: Public websites, Documents, SharePoint, Dataverse, Enterprise data using connectors.
  4. Allow ungrounded responses setting manages whether the agent can generate responses using only the model's general knowledge.
  5. Official sources mark a knowledge sources to be highly trusted and can be used directly by the agent without verification but generative orchestration needs to be turned off.
  6. All knowledge sources added at agent level are added to the generative answers node in Conversational boosting system topic.

Everything tools

  1. Tools let agent interact with external systems.
  2. Tools: Connectors, Agent flow, Prompt, REST API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Computer use with GUI.
  3. Agent flow response: a. Dont respond (default) b. Write the response with generative AI c. Send specific response d. Send an adaptive card

Multi-agent solution

  1. Agents can hand off user interactions to each other or respond to autonomous triggers.
  2. Ways to add other agent: a. Create child agents b. Connect to other Copilot Studio agents within same environment c. Connect to external agents: Over A2A protocol, Foundry agents, Fabric Data agents, Microsoft 365 Agents SDK.
  3. Potential impact: Increased latency due to extra orchestration hops, Increased testing, management and governance surface area.
  4. Use 'Add an agent' node to redirect to an agent from a topic.
  5. Issues: introduces a slightly longer execution time due to context switching, complexity in maintaining multiple agents.
  6. Best practices: a. Ensure only one agent talk to the user. Only the parent agent should deliver the final response. b. Always tell subagents that they are sub agents as sub agents inherently dont know they are part of an orchestration. c. Use clear, direct language in instructions. Avoid soft phrasing like "please", "try to", "you should" but instead use strong language like "MUST", "DO NOT", "NEVER". d. Use one knowledge source per subagent. e. Write clear, distinct descriptions for each subagent visible to the parent. The parent agent uses subagent descriptions to decide routing. f. Tell the parent agent how to orchestrate. The parent needs explicit instructions on the pattern: invoke agents, wait for results, combine, then respond. g.

Limitations

  1. The description can have up to 1024 characters.
  2. Node names can be up to 500 characters in length.
  3. Avoid using periods (.) in your topic names. It isn't possible to export a solution.
  4. Text file to upload trigger phrases should be max 3 MB.
  5. Under knowledge sources: 25 websites under generative mode while 4 public URLs in classic mode.
  6. Under knowledge source: All/Any documents under generative mode while Dataverse file storage under classic mode
  7. Under knowledge source: Unlimited Dataverse under generative mode while 2 Dataverse knowledge source (15 tables per knowledge source) under classic mode.
  8. Under knowledge source: Unlimited connectors under generative mode while 2 per custom agent in classic mode.
  9. In knowledge source, the agent only shows content that the specific user can access.
  10. File uploads to agent are limited to 15 MB.
  11. Agent flow must respond to the agent within the 100-second action limit.
  12. Under generative mode, the orchestrator supports up to 128 tools per agent. For best performance, limit to 25-30 tools.

AI Fundamentals

  • Cloud Platform: A cloud platform is a collection of services that can be used over the Internet instead of running it on computer or server.

  • Azure core categories: Compute, Storage, Networking, App Services.

  • Azure organization structure: Tenants -> Subscription -> Resource group and resources

  • Azure Tenant: It is an organization's home base and identity in Microsoft's cloud. The tenant includes users, groups, identities and policies for managing secure access.

  • Azure Subscription: A billing container for cloud resources. One tenant can contain one or many Azure subscriptions. Its tied with a payment method and sets boundaries for cost, quotas and access control.

  • Resource groups: Resource groups are folder that hold related Azure resources to manage them together.

  • Resource: Any individual service or object created in Azure. Each resource has resource type, configuration settings, unique resource name and ID and optional access controls.

  • Azure Portal: Open 'portal.azure.com' is a centrallized, web-based management user interface.

  • Host: Applications run on computers or environments. A host can be a virtual machine, provide compute, memory and networking to execute.

  • Scaling: To automatically or manually adjust the amount of computer power to use by adding or removing instances.

  • Instances: Copies of application running at the same time.

  • Types of scaling: Scale out or horizontal - to add more instances | Scale up or vertical - to increase CPU/memory on existing instance

AI Types of Data

  • Training data: Data that teaches the AI model patterns.

  • Inference input data: the real-time user or system input.

  • AI model output data: predictions or generated responses.

  • Application state: data that supports user-specific continuity

  • System/ config data: supports how the AI app behaves

  • Logs & telemetry: monitoring and optimization

  • Security & access data: safe authentication and authorization

Microsoft Foundry for AI

  • When an agent queries the knowledge base, Foundry IQ uses agentic retrieval to break the question into subqueries, search multiple sources in parallel and return relevant, citation-backed information.

  • A foundry project builds and manages: Agents | Evaluations | Files and datasets | Vector indexes | Flows | Connections | Project-specific settings.

  • Two endpoints in Foundry: Project-level endpoints, Model endpoints

Client-Server Interaction

  • A client application is a program that a user interacts with on their device that sends requests to a server and displays the results.

  • An AI client application utilizes a model, data, and application logic to process and return results. The app logic is the code or workflow that sends requests to the model, receives the response, and processes and transforms results. The entire process is known as a client–server interaction.

entry.title: Adaptive Cards
entry.content:
Adaptive Cards

  • Adaptive cards are snippets of UI created in JSON.
  • The JSON is transformed into native UI.
  • It helps design and integrate light-weight UI for all major platforms and frameworks.

Goals of Adaptive Card

  1. Portable to any app, device or UI framework
  2. Open: Libraries and schema are open source and shared
  3. Low cost: Easy to define, easy to consume
  4. Expressive
  5. Purely declarative: No code is needed
  6. Automatically styled

Card Layouts

  1. Hero: Ideal for sharing articles where an image tells most of the story.
  2. Thumbnail: for quick interactions
  3. List: to pick an item from a list
  4. Digest: for news digests or round-up posts
  5. Video/Media: Combines text and media
  6. Form: to collect quick inputs from users to create tasks
  7. Quick Input: to collect quick inputs from users
  8. Expandable: allows users to select buttons and gather additional input from the same card.

Collapisble Sections

  • Action.ShowCard and Action.ToggleVisibility to show information dynamically.

Container Layouts

  1. Layout.Stack: stacks elements on top of each other. Used by default.
  2. Layout.Flow: spreads elements horizontally and wraps them across multiple rows as needed.
  3. Layout.AreaGrid: divides a container into named areas into which elements can be placed.

Elements:

  1. ActionSet: Displays a set of action, which can be placed anywhere in the card.
  2. Table
  3. Progressar
  4. ImageSet
  5. Image
  6. Icon
  7. FactSet
  8. Container: to logically group a set of elements together, A container for other elements.
  9. TextBlock:

Actions

  1. Action.Execute
  2. Action.InsertImage
  3. Action.OpenUrl
  4. Action.OpenUrlDialog
  5. Action.Popover
  6. Action.ResetInputs
  7. Action.ShowCard
  8. Action.Submit
  9. Action.ToggleVisibilty

Inputs

  1. Input.ChoiceSet
  2. Input.Date
  3. Input.Number
  4. Input.Rating
  5. Input.Text
  6. Input.Time
  7. Input.Toggle

entry.title: Interview Topics in Detail
entry.content:
Autonomous Agent

  • Autonomous agents in Copilot Studio extend the value of generative orchestration by enabling AI to take action without waiting for a user prompt.
  • These agents perceive events, make decisions, and execute tasks independently by using triggers, instructions, and guardrails you define.
  • Instead of responding only in conversations, they operate continuously in the background—monitoring data, reacting to conditions, and running workflows at scale.

Semi-autonomous Agent

  • A semi-autonomous agent works similarly, but it pauses to check in with a human for approval before taking any important action.

Generative Orchestration

  • Generative orchestration lets your custom agent answer user queries with relevant topics, tools, other agents, and knowledge sources, and respond to event triggers.
  • Generative orchestration builds a plan to address a user query or event trigger using the name, description, inputs, and outputs of available topics, tools, agents, and knowledge.
  • For conversations, the system references the last 10 turns of conversation history to fill in inputs.
  • Link (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/faqs-generative-orchestration)

Copilot Foundational Elements

  1. Knowledge: Allows the agent to use predefined documents, FAQs, or external data sources to provide instructions for the agent to respond.
  2. Topics: Manages the conversation flows by defining intents, triggers, and responses for user queries.
  3. Actions: Defines what the agent can do, such as triggering an action or workflow, calling an API, sending an email, or integrating with external systems to trigger an external workflow.
  4. Triggers: Event-based starting points that initiate an automated flow, which help define specific conditions that activate specific actions.
  5. Activity: Tracks and logs interactions, providing visibility into user engagement with the agent.
  6. Analytics: Provides insights and performance metrics on agent usage, effectiveness, and user interactions.
  7. Channels: Configures deployment options, which allows the agent to be accessible on various platforms like Microsoft Teams or internal and external websites.

System Topic

  • System topics support essential behaviors, such as a custom request to speak to a person or end the conversation.
  • You can't create or delete system topics, but you can turn them off.

Custom Topic

  • The predefined custom topics cover common behaviors, such as greeting a customer, ending a conversation, or restarting conversation.
  • You can make changes to the predefined custom topics or remove them from your agent entirely.

Trigger Phrases

  • Trigger phrases indicate to the agent what typical user utterances should trigger a specific topic.

entry.title: Admin Cost Governance
entry.content:
Role of Admins

  • Admins watch the same Copilot Credit consumption.
  • They fund the capacity
  • Govern how the capacity is shared and used.
  • Copilot Credits are pooled at tenant level.

Funding models

  • Pay-as-you-go: Usage is billed to an Azure subscription after the billing month. There is no upfront commitment.
  • Prepaid capacity: Organization purchase Copilot Credit packs in advance. There is an upfront commitment. Credits are bought before consumed.

Admins that govern

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Power Platform admin center

entry.title: Model Context Protocol
entry.content:
Model Context Protocol or MCP

  • MCP is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.
  • It enables them to access key information and perform tasks.
  • In Copilot Studio, it allows makers to integrate existing knowledge servers and APIs directly.

What can MCP do?

  • Agents can access Google calendar becoming a more personalized AI assistant.
  • Claude Code can generate an entire web app using Figma design.
  • Enterprise chatbots can connect to multiple databases across an organization.
